studies.label: Online experiment with professionals: occupation-specific writing with ChatGPT versus Overleaf signup

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Method, recruitment; PDF p. 18, Table 1; PDF p. 19, Table 1 note
counts_source.quote: we recruited 453 experienced, college-educated professionals on the survey platform Prolific and assigned each to complete two occupation-specific, incentivized writing tasks (21).

arms.name: Treatment (ChatGPT)
arms.description: After the pre-intervention writing task, participants were instructed to register for ChatGPT, received guidance, and could use it on the second task. Assignment was to access and encouragement, with optional use (PDF p. 3, Method).

arms.name: Control (Overleaf signup)
arms.description: Registered for Overleaf to match signup time and hassle, without being told they could use it on the second task. This is the no-assigned-AI control, not an active writing-aid intervention. Some control participants independently used ChatGPT (PDF p. 3, Method; PDF p. 4, Takeup of ChatGPT).

studies.task: Professionals completed occupation-specific writing tasks, including press releases, short reports, analysis plans, and delicate emails, before and after the signup intervention.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3, Method: GPT-3.5 is named and the experiment is dated January 27 to February 21, 2023; no model release year is stated, so year is null.

preregistration.where: AEA RCT Registry, https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/10882; DOI 10.1257/rct.10882-2.1 (PDF p. 11, Data and materials availability).

estimates.outcome: Average evaluator grade: pooled main incentive schemes, Figure 1
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Blinded experienced professionals working in the same occupations scored the produced writing on a 1-7 scale; each output was seen by three evaluators. The saved manuscript does not supply a grade-specific rubric or explain the aggregation across grade dimensions. Figure 1B uses participant-evaluator observations of pre-to-post grade changes. Figure 1D prints raw post-treatment grade means at the same participant-evaluator level.

regression.model: Regression of within-participant pre-to-post grade change on a treatment dummy, occupation*task-order fixed effects, incentive-arm fixed effects, and grader fixed effects, at the participant-evaluator level. Standard errors are clustered by person. The displayed coefficient and confidence interval are rescaled to pre-treatment standard deviations of the outcome variable; the unscaled coefficient and its SE are not printed.

estimates.notes: Retained as the paper's pooled main specification across the linear and convex incentive schemes; it excludes the separate fixed-time incentive group and is not an estimate over every recruited participant. The grade means are raw post-treatment rating means, whereas the regression coefficient and its confidence interval are adjusted change-score effects expressed in baseline outcome SD units. No mean difference, SD, SE, or graph coordinates were calculated. Only printed figure annotations were transcribed. The paper does not state whether the baseline standardizer is a control-arm or pooled SD, or whether it is computed across ratings or participant means; sd_level is therefore null. Person-clustered uncertainty qualifies as participant-based even though unit is rating. The prose effect is recorded separately because its value differs and its exact sample/model is not identified. The repeated task measurements are baseline adjustment in a between-person randomized experiment, not a randomized crossover.

estimates.notes: The prose reports an effect in standard-deviation units without naming it Cohen's d, Hedges' g, or a standardized beta, so paper_effect.type is other. It does not separately identify the sample, denominator, analysis unit, or uncertainty model behind this number. The Figure 1 specification and confidence interval are not transferred to this record. The abstract additionally summarizes output quality as an 18% increase; that alternative expression of the same outcome is preserved here, not treated as another independent contrast or converted into a proportion. This is a work-quality outcome, not an overall-creativity rating. No grade-specific effect or p-value is inferred from this average-grade result.

open_items: Exact numbers randomized and analyzed, overall and by arm/outcome, are not explicitly established. The recruitment count and Table 1 descriptive/baseline Ns do not identify the post-treatment regression samples. No counts were inferred by adding table entries, applying percentages, or using degrees of freedom (PDF p. 3, Method; PDF pp. 18-19, Table 1).

The sample/model responsible for the main-text average-grade effect differs or is otherwise unexplained relative to the Figure 1 annotation. Whether the prose effect covers the fixed-time group is not stated. The two printed results remain separate (PDF p. 4, Productivity; PDF p. 12, Figure 1B).

Figure 1 provides neither participant-level arm SDs nor a numerical baseline SD. The level and arm composition of the pre-treatment SD standardizer, the raw adjusted coefficient, and its SE are not reported (PDF p. 12, Figure 1 note).

Originality, overall grade, writing-quality grade, and content-quality grade each lack outcome-specific numerical results, uncertainty, analysis units, and counts. The average-grade result must not be substituted for any of them (PDF p. 4, Productivity).

The separate Supplementary Materials are referenced but absent from the saved PDF and the local supplement manifest has no files. They may contain grade-specific analyses, scoring rubrics, exact counts, Lee bounds, additional controls, and compliance-adjusted estimates. None of these supplementary results could be verified.

The manuscript names its preregistration but does not state a preregistered primary outcome; primary-outcome status remains not_stated. The registry itself was not consulted (PDF p. 11, Data and materials availability).
Participant country and the AI model release year are not stated in the saved manuscript. The experiment date is not used as a model release date (PDF p. 3, Method).
notes: The entire markdown conversion, including references, notes, figures, and the closing table, was read sequentially; text from every PDF page was then extracted with pymupdf, and Table 1 was checked with find_tables(). PDF page numbers match the printed page numbers. Only this extraction file was written. This is one between-person randomized experiment with pre-intervention task measurements, not a randomized within-person order design. The general work-quality grades are coded usefulness and originality is coded novelty, following their definitions and the reconciled screening map. No cross-person content-diversity outcome or scored unassisted post-AI outcome is reported. No shared sample with another paper is disclosed. The pooled main-incentive Figure 1 specification is retained with its sample restriction explicit; the separate fixed-time incentive robustness subgroup is excluded. Abstract percentage wording is documented as an alternative summary, not an independent effect. Access to the named OSF API endpoints https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/xd7qw/files/osfstorage/ and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/xd7qw/files/ was attempted with urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1; both failed with a socket-permission error, so no external supplement or data were used. No statistics were computed.
